items.followUp: Explain how water and minerals are transported from roots to leaves.

rubric.why: Checks that the student names the tissue and process involved in food transport.
rubric.description: Food is transported through the phloem by translocation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both phloem and translocation.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the cells involved in phloem transport.
rubric.description: Phloem contains sieve tubes associated with companion cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming sieve tubes and companion cells.

rubric.why: Checks how food enters the phloem at a source.
rubric.description: Sugars are actively loaded into the phloem at a source, such as a leaf.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that sugars are actively loaded into the phloem.

rubric.why: Checks how water enters the phloem and contributes to pressure.
rubric.description: Water enters the phloem from the xylem by osmosis, increasing pressure in the sieve tubes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking water entry into the phloem with osmosis.

rubric.why: Checks movement towards sinks and release of sugars there.
rubric.description: Pressure moves phloem sap towards sinks, where sugars are unloaded.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing pressure-driven movement towards sinks and sugar unloading.

modelAnswer: Food is transported through the phloem by a process called translocation.
Phloem contains sieve tubes associated with companion cells.
At a source, such as a leaf, sugars are actively loaded into the phloem.
Water enters the phloem from the xylem by osmosis, increasing pressure in the sieve tubes.
This pressure moves phloem sap towards sinks, such as roots or growing parts, where sugars are unloaded; water can return to the xylem.

rubric.why: Checks the substance moved, membrane, and direction of osmosis.
rubric.description: Osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining osmosis with water moving through a selectively permeable membrane from dilute to more concentrated solution.

rubric.why: Checks the direction and energy requirement of active transport.
rubric.description: Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient using energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that active transport uses energy to move substances against the concentration gradient.

modelAnswer: Osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution.
Active transport is the movement of substances against their concentration gradient using energy.
